subject: Annual renewal: rightsizing proposal & hybrid credit swap
messages:
From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@marketly.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@marketly.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — rightsizing + credit ask

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the renewal overview last week. We pulled together usage through Q2 and there are two things we'd like to propose ahead of the June renewal:

1) Rightsizing: actual runtime for our inference workloads has flattened; we expect a 10-15% lower sustained token throughput vs the commit in our current contract.
2) Short-term surge coverage: we still anticipate spikes around product launches and want to avoid throttling.

From Marketly's side we want to propose a hybrid approach: reduce the committed baseline by 12% for year 1 (rightsized to realistic steady-state), but in exchange take a 30% credit pool that can be drawn for bursts and applied to overage invoices. That preserves revenue for Redwood while protecting us during launches.

Attached is our Q2 usage summary and a redline of the renewal blackline for reference. Can your team run numbers on how a 12% commit reduction plus a 30% drawdown credit pool would impact unit economics and invoice timing?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming for a July 10 signature window.

Best,
Evelyn
Head of Platform Ops
Marketly

Attachment stubs: Marketly_usage_summary_Q2.xlsx (xlsx, 130KB), Marketly_Renewal_Blackline_2028.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

-----Original Message-----

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@marketly.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — rightsizing + credit ask

Evelyn — thanks for the summary and the attachments. I reviewed the usage sheet with David and Ben this morning. Quick take: your steady-state projection maps to a sustainable commit reduction, but the credit pool structure needs clarity on draw mechanics, expiry, and accounting (how credits reduce overage vs future invoice credits).

Prelim options from Redwood: 
- Option A (Rightsize + credit pool): 12% commit reduction, 30% convertible credit pool valid 12 months; credits apply first to overage on a prorated basis. Estimated net-first-year revenue impact: -6% vs current ARR (includes projected burst drawdown).
- Option B (Rightsize + price hold): 12% commit reduction, no credit pool, 6-month price hold on per-token rates for bursts up to 150% of baseline; net-first-year revenue impact: -3%.
- Option C (Conservative): Keep current commit, provide a one-time operational credit equal to 10% of one quarter invoice to cover an expected launch spike; net-first-year revenue impact: +1% (favors Redwood stability).

Can you confirm which option is closest to Marketly's appetite? If you prefer Option A we'll need Monica to model the credit ledger and Ben to confirm runtime impact on our batch/kv caching assumptions during spikes.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync next week.

— Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — rightsizing + credit ask

Quick ops note: if Marketly reduces baseline commit by ~12% and expects burst coverage to 150-200% of baseline, we can support that with a combination of burst pool + cache-priority tuning. Two practical constraints: 
1) Burst drawdown that spins GPUs from cold will increase per-token cost during the spike — the credit pool size needs to be sized to cover both volume and higher unit cost.
2) If credits are refundable/convertible into future invoices, we need a clean accounting treatment in the contract (timing of recognition).

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood

>

> - Option A (12% commit down + 30% credit pool): Gross margin falls ~9% in Y1 but improves in Y2 due to lower baseline.
> - Option B (12% commit down + 6mo price hold): Margin impact ~-4% in Y1; risk of repeated short holds drives complexity for ops.
> - Option C (no commit change + one-time credit): Most predictable for revenue recognition; lowest churn risk but Marketly carries higher short-term price exposure.

If Marketly is prioritizing invoice predictability + avoiding procurement back-and-forth, Option B is often the fastest to close. If preserving long-term unit economics for Marketly's product team is the priority, Option A with a strict 12-month expiry on credits makes sense.

-----Original Message-----

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>; Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@marketly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>; David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — rightsizing + credit ask

Thanks all. To make Option A operationally viable we recommend the following contractual language and mechanics: 

- Credit pool: fixed dollar amount equal to 30% of expected annualized spend under the rightsized commit. Draws are consumed first against monthly overage invoices; any remaining credit can be applied to the following month invoice but expires at 12 months.
- Draw limits: single-draw cap to prevent a single launch from exhausting credits immediately (recommend 25% of the pool per month).
- Reporting: Marketly must submit a launch notice (72-hour window) to qualify for credit-protected bursts above 150% of baseline — this avoids gaming.
- Accounting: Credits will be recorded as a contract liability and amortized over 12 months where applicable; Redwood retains rights to audit draw claims for the first two draws.

I attached a snip of proposed contract language (attached to my note) and a sample amortization schedule. If Marketly accepts these guardrails we can finalize the SOW and route to legal for a clause insert.

Monica
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Next steps I propose:
